Uniform approximation

 Home Mathematics Area of mathematics Analysis
OurBigBook.com Words: 7k Articles: 118
Uniform approximation minimizes the supremum norm of the difference between a target function and an approximant.
The error is measured uniformly over the domain using the supremum norm. A sequence of approximants whose uniform error tends to zero converges by uniform convergence; the optimization problem and the convergence notion are distinct.

Lebesgue constant of interpolation (Λx​=maxt​∑i​∣ℓi​(t)∣)

Words: 142 Articles: 1
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
If interpolation at distinct sites xi​ in a finite-dimensional space of continuous functions is unique, its cardinal functions satisfy ℓi​(xj​)=δij​. The interpolation linear map is Pf=∑i​f(xi​)ℓi​ and has operator norm Λx​ in the supremum norm. The upper bound is the triangle inequality. For the reverse bound choose node values to be the signs of the cardinal functions at a point maximizing their absolute sum, and extend those values by a continuous function of norm one. The polynomial reproduction error bound gives ∥f−Pf∥∞​≤(1+Λx​)infs∈rangeP​∥f−s∥∞​.

Fekete interpolation sites for a continuous function space (maxx1​,…,xn​​∣det(ϕj​(xi​))∣)

Words: 71
Lebesgue constant of interpolation OurBigBook.com
For a real n-dimensional vector space of continuous functions on a compact interval, choose sites maximizing the absolute evaluation determinant in any basis. Linear independence ensures some nonzero evaluation determinant, so a maximizer exists and has distinct sites. Replacing row i by evaluation at t multiplies the determinant by the cardinal function ℓi​(t). Maximality implies ∣ℓi​(t)∣≤1, hence the Lebesgue constant of interpolation is at most n. This gives a useful interpolation set without asserting that determinant maximization minimizes the Lebesgue constant of interpolation.

Chebyshev system (Φ=(u0​,…,un​))

Words: 245 Articles: 3
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
A Chebyshev system on a nondegenerate real interval is a family of n+1 real continuous functions such that every linear combination with coefficients not all zero has at most n distinct zeros. The condition entails linear independence and unique interpolation at any n+1 distinct points. It is a zero-counting hypothesis, not a requirement to count multiplicities.

Odd dimension of a periodic Chebyshev system

Words: 72
Chebyshev system OurBigBook.com
A Chebyshev system of real continuous functions on a circle has odd dimension. If its dimension is d, take d cyclically ordered evaluation points and move them continuously to the next cyclic permutation without letting points collide. The evaluation determinant stays nonzero, so cannot change sign. The final cyclic row permutation multiplies it by (−1)d−1; consequently d must be odd. For example, 1,cosx,sinx,…,cosmx,sinmx has dimension 2m+1 and the required zero bound.

Exponential Chebyshev system (eλ0​x,…,eλn​x)

Words: 65
Chebyshev system OurBigBook.com
Exponentials with distinct real exponents form a Chebyshev system on every nondegenerate real interval. For an inductive proof, multiply a candidate combination by e−λ0​x. If it has n+1 zeros, Rolle's theorem gives at least n zeros of its derivative, a combination of the n exponentials with exponents λi​−λ0​, i>0. The inductive zero bound forces all those coefficients to vanish. The remaining constant also vanishes, a contradiction.

Determinant criterion for a Chebyshev system (det(uj​(xi​))=0)

Words: 58
Chebyshev system OurBigBook.com
A family of n+1 real continuous functions is a Chebyshev system exactly when every evaluation matrix at n+1 distinct points is invertible. A singular evaluation matrix supplies a nonzero coefficient vector whose function vanishes at those points; conversely, a violation of the zero bound supplies such a vector in the kernel. This also gives the existence and uniqueness of interpolation from its span.

Uniform closure of a function algebra

Words: 56
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
For an algebra A⊆C(K) on a compact space, its uniform closure consists of functions that are uniform limits of sequences from A. It is a closed algebra in the uniform norm, because addition and multiplication preserve uniform convergence for bounded functions. If it contains every constant and separates points, the Stone-Weierstrass theorem makes the closure all of C(K).

Integer polynomial approximation away from zero and one

Words: 62
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
On [a,b]⊂(0,1), the uniform closure of integer-coefficient polynomials contains 1/2, since ∑j=0N​x(1−2x)j→1/2 uniformly. This closure is a ring, so it contains all dyadic constants and then all real constants. It contains x and therefore every real-coefficient polynomial. The Stone-Weierstrass theorem makes it all of C([a,b]). On an interval including zero this fails, since the value of an integer-coefficient polynomial at zero is an integer.

Polynomial approximation (En​(f)=infdegp≤n​∥f−p∥∞​)

Words: 115 Articles: 1
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
Polynomial approximation represents a function by polynomials of bounded polynomial degree. On a compact real interval, the Weierstrass approximation theorem guarantees uniform approximation of every continuous function by such polynomials. The displayed best error quantifies the accuracy available at degree at most n.

Strict polynomial error decrease from nonvanishing derivatives (En−1​(f)>En​(f))

Words: 80
Polynomial approximation OurBigBook.com
If n≥1, f is real and Cn on an interval, and f(n) is nowhere zero there, the displayed inequality holds. If the errors were equal, a best degree-at-most-n−1 polynomial would also be best at degree n. The Chebyshev alternation theorem and intermediate value theorem would give n+1 zeros of the error. Applying Rolle's theorem n times would force a zero of f(n), a contradiction. The zero-error case already contradicts f(n)=0. In particular this proves strict improvement for the exponential function at every positive degree step.

Bernstein inequality for algebraic polynomials (∣p′(x)∣≤n∥p∥[−1,1]​/1−x2​)

Words: 255 Articles: 3
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
For a polynomial of degree at most n, this derivative estimate holds for −1<x<1. It controls the derivative away from the endpoints. Sampling it at Chebyshev polynomial roots supplies the hypotheses of the Chebyshev nodal derivative comparison, which controls the missing endpoint regions. The norm is taken on the entire interval, although the displayed pointwise bound concerns its interior.

Markov inequality for polynomial derivatives (∥p′∥[−1,1]​≤n2∥p∥[−1,1]​)

Words: 200 Articles: 2
Bernstein inequality for algebraic polynomials OurBigBook.com
Apply the Bernstein inequality for algebraic polynomials to the central interval ∣x∣≤cos(π/(2n)), using sin(π/(2n))≥1/n. On the remaining regions apply the Chebyshev nodal derivative comparison to p′. Since Tn′​(cosθ)=nsin(nθ)/sinθ, the identity expressing sin(nθ)/sinθ as a sum of n unit complex phases gives ∣Tn′​∣≤n2. The endpoint limit is Tn′​(1)=n2, so the constant is sharp.

Duffin-Schaeffer polynomial derivative inequality (∥p(k)∥∞​≤Tn(k)​(1))

Words: 150 Articles: 1
Markov inequality for polynomial derivatives OurBigBook.com
If a real degree-at-most-n polynomial has absolute value at most one at every extremum cos(jπ/n) of the Chebyshev polynomial Tn​, its kth derivative on [−1,1] is bounded by Tn(k)​(1), for 1≤k≤n. This strengthens the Markov inequality for polynomial derivatives by replacing a bound on the whole interval with these finitely many samples. The node set is rigid, as quantified by uniqueness of Chebyshev derivative-norming nodes.
Uniqueness of Chebyshev derivative-norming nodes (q(k)(1)>Tn(k)​(1),1≤k≤n)
Words: 91
Duffin-Schaeffer polynomial derivative inequality OurBigBook.com
For n≥1, any distinct node set in [−1,1] different from the n+1 Chebyshev polynomial extrema admits one degree-n polynomial q, bounded by one at all those nodes, whose every nonconstant derivative violates the corresponding sharp endpoint bound. In decreasing order set q(ti​)=(−1)i. The endpoint derivative signs of Lagrange cardinal polynomials give q(k)(1)=∑i​∣Li(k)​(1)∣. Interpolating Tn​ on the same nodes shows
q(k)(1)−Tn(k)​(1)=∑i​∣Li(k)​(1)∣[1−(−1)iTn​(ti​)]>0.
(1)
Each term is nonnegative and at least one is positive, because the other node set includes a nonextremal point. Uniqueness is a claim about node sets: permuting the same nodes does not change their norming property.

Extension of approximation operators from a dense subspace (∥Tn​f−f∥≤(C+1)∥f−p∥+∥Tn​p−p∥)

Words: 54
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
Suppose linear operators Tn​ on a normed vector space satisfy ∥Tn​∥≤C uniformly and Tn​p→p on a dense subspace. The displayed triangle inequality for any element p of that subspace first permits p to approximate f, then lets n increase, proving Tn​f→f for every f. Applied to the Bernstein polynomial, the Weierstrass approximation theorem supplies the dense polynomial subspace and C=1.

Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem

Words: 335 Articles: 2
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
Every real continuous function on a compact square can be represented as ∑q=15​Gq​(aq​(x)+bq​(y)), with continuous one-variable functions and fixed inner functions aq​,bq​ independent of the represented function. Grid-separated additive coordinates give the inner functions. For a residual r of norm M, assign r at a sample point divided by three to each separated rectangle image, and continuously interpolate between images. Each point lies in at least three rectangles, so if k∈{3,4,5} summands are accurate, the error is at most [∣1−k/3∣+(5−k)/3]M+5η/3=2M/3+5η/3. Choose oscillation η≤M/10 to obtain contraction 5/6. Iteration gives outer functions by uniform convergence of corrections bounded by M(5/6)j/3. Whole-plane reduction for continuous superposition removes compactness of the original domain without assuming boundedness of the original function.

Whole-plane reduction for continuous superposition

Words: 82
Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem OurBigBook.com
For f∈C(R2), choose a positive continuous function A with A(t)≥(1+t)maxx2+y2≤t​∣f(x,y)∣ for t≥0. Such an A is obtained by piecewise linear interpolation of a sufficiently large increasing sequence. Then b(x,y)=f(x,y)/A(x2+y2) tends uniformly to zero at infinity. Transport b to (0,1)2 by x=tan(π(s−1/2)) and extend it by zero on the boundary; the extension is continuous. Apply the compact Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, then multiply by A(x2+y2). Multiplication introduces no additional primitive operation because uv=[(u+v)2−(u−v)2]/4 uses only addition and continuous one-variable squaring and scaling.

Grid-separated additive coordinates

Words: 142
Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem OurBigBook.com
For five pairs of continuous functions on [0,1], one can arrange that at every arbitrarily fine scale there are closed interval families whose product rectangles cover each point at least three times, and within each family the images under aq​(x)+bq​(y) are mutually disjoint. To see this, put gaps near five shifted fine grids; gap sets for different shifts are disjoint. Each coordinate misses at most one family, so a pair misses at most two. Approximate any prescribed pair of functions by constants on the complementary intervals, interpolating across gaps. Perturb the finitely many constants to avoid all equalities between distinct pair sums. The rectangle images are then separated by a positive distance, a property preserved under sufficiently small uniform perturbations. For each required mesh size this property defines a dense open subset of C([0,1])10. The Baire category theorem gives a tuple satisfying every scale simultaneously.

pN​(z)=−ζ−c1​∑j=0N​(ζ−cz−c​)j

Moving an exterior pole to obtain pointwise polynomial approximation (pn​(z)→(z−z0​)−1)

Words: 78
Polynomial approximation of an exterior pole on a convex compact set OurBigBook.com
Let z0​ be a boundary point of a compact convex set and choose exterior points ζn​→z0​. Approximate (z−ζn​)−1 uniformly on the compact set by a polynomial with error at most 1/n. At each fixed z=z0​, the reciprocal converges and so does the approximating polynomial. On a boundary accumulating at z0​, uniform convergence to the singular reciprocal is impossible because each polynomial is bounded there. This distinguishes pointwise convergence from uniform convergence without confusing the two norms.

Integer-coefficient polynomial approximation (Z[x]​∥⋅∥∞​={f∈C[0,1]:f(0),f(1)∈Z})

Words: 52
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
The uniform approximation closure of the integer-coefficient polynomials on [0,1] consists precisely of the continuous functions taking integer values at both endpoints. Necessity follows because evaluations at zero and one are integers and convergent integer sequences are eventually constant. For sufficiency, the rounded Bernstein polynomial has integer monomial coefficients and differs uniformly by a vanishing amount from the Bernstein polynomial, which converges uniformly to the target.

For a continuous periodic function set
ω2​(f,h)=sup∣u∣≤h​∥f(⋅+u)−2f+f(⋅−u)∥∞​.
(3)

f(x+h)−2f(x)+f(x−h)=∫−hh​(h−∣u∣)f′′(x+u)du.
(4)

Uniform step approximation on a compact interval (∥f−g∥∞​≤Lh)

Words: 69
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
A uniformly continuous real function on a closed bounded interval can be approximated uniformly by finite step functions. Given ε>0, choose a mesh smaller than the uniform-continuity distance and set the approximant equal to a sampled value on each interval. Then the supremum norm of the approximation error is at most ε. If the function has a Lipschitz bound L, a mesh of maximum length h gives the explicit error bound ∥f−g∥∞​≤Lh.

Cosine substitution for polynomial approximation (f​(θ)=f(cosθ))

Words: 61
Best uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
Cosine substitution is an isometry from continuous functions on [−1,1] to even continuous 2π-periodic functions. It satisfies ω(f​,δ)≤ω(f,δ) because cosine is Lipschitz continuous with constant one. Even degree-at-most-n trigonometric polynomials correspond exactly to algebraic polynomials via Tj​(cosθ)=cos(jθ). Averaging a periodic approximant with its reflection cannot increase its error against an even target, so the algebraic and periodic best errors are equal.

Polynomial reproduction error bound (∥f−Pf∥≤(1+∥P∥)EV​(f))

Words: 48
Best uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
If a bounded linear map P reproduces every element of an approximating polynomial space V, then f−Pf=(f−v)−P(f−v) for every v∈V. The triangle inequality and infimum over v prove the displayed error bound. The same argument works for any linear approximating space, and applies in particular to de la Vallée Poussin sums.

Uniqueness of best uniform polynomial approximation

Words: 62
Best uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
For a fixed degree bound, two best approximating polynomials have a best approximating average. At each active point of that average their errors agree, hence the two polynomials agree. There must be at least two more active points than the degree: otherwise polynomial interpolation constructs a strictly improving sign-matching perturbation. The difference has too many zeros and must vanish. Finite-dimensional coefficient compactness also gives existence.

Kolmogorov criterion for uniform approximation

Words: 66
Best uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
For real f, a candidate u∈U⊂C(K,R), and active set E={x:∣f(x)−u(x)∣=∥f−u∥∞​}, the candidate is best precisely when every v∈U has some x∈E with (f(x)−u(x))v(x)≤0. A direction with strictly matching error signs on the whole active set gives a uniformly improving small perturbation by compactness. Conversely one oppositely signed active value already prevents improvement. This criterion yields the Chebyshev alternation theorem.

Equioscillation theorem

Words: 446 Articles: 6
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
A degree-at-most-m polynomial is a best uniform approximation precisely when its error attains alternating extrema of equal magnitude at at least m+2 ordered points.

Strict decrease of best polynomial approximation under a derivative sign (f(n+1)>0⟹En​(f)>En+1​(f))

Words: 70
Equioscillation theorem OurBigBook.com
For real f∈Cn+1[0,1] with positive (n+1)st derivative, equality of consecutive best uniform approximation errors would make a best degree-at-most-n polynomial also best at degree n+1. The Chebyshev alternation theorem then supplies n+3 alternating extrema of its nonzero error, hence n+2 distinct zeros. Repeated Rolle's theorem forces a zero of the (n+1)st derivative of that error, contradicting the assumed sign. The same conclusion holds for a strictly negative derivative by replacing f with −f.

Trigonometric Chebyshev alternation theorem (2n+2 alternating extrema)

Words: 275 Articles: 3
Equioscillation theorem OurBigBook.com
For real continuous 2π-periodic f, a degree-at-most-n real trigonometric polynomial p is its unique best uniform approximation exactly when f−p has 2n+2 alternating extrema of magnitude ∥f−p∥∞​ at distinct ordered points in one period. The closing interval around the circle also counts. A strictly improving approximant would force its difference from p to have at least 2n+2 zeros, whereas a nonzero degree-n trigonometric polynomial has at most 2n.

Positive lacunary trigonometric series (En​(f)=∑qk>n​ak​)

Words: 210 Articles: 2
Trigonometric Chebyshev alternation theorem OurBigBook.com
For an odd integer q≥3 and positive summable coefficients ak​, the Weierstrass M-test makes f(x)=∑k≥0​ak​cos(qkx) continuous. Its partial sum over qk≤n is the unique best uniform approximation by degree-at-most-n trigonometric polynomials, for n≥1. If Q is the first omitted frequency, at xj​=jπ/Q every omitted cosine equals (−1)j because all frequency ratios are odd. Thus the tail attains alternating extrema equal to its coefficient sum at 2Q≥2n+2 points. The trigonometric Chebyshev alternation theorem proves the formula. For ak​=r−k, r>1, the largest decay exponent is logr/logq.
Weierstrass function (ga,b​(x)=∑k≥0​a−kcos(bkx))
Words: 129 Articles: 1
Positive lacunary trigonometric series OurBigBook.com
A standard Weierstrass function is a uniformly convergent lacunary cosine series, here parameterized by a>1 and an integer frequency multiplier b>1. Its continuity follows from the Weierstrass M-test. In the range 1<a<b, its modulus of continuity has the fractional-power scale δloga/logb for the positive odd-frequency model; the critical case a=b can have the larger scale δlog(1/δ). These examples distinguish small approximation error from ordinary Lipschitz continuity.
Critical Weierstrass modulus (ω(g5,5​,δ)≍δlog(1/δ))
Words: 65
Weierstrass function OurBigBook.com
For g(x)=∑k≥0​5−kcos(5kx), all frequencies satisfy 5k≡1(mod4). At x=π/2, the increment is −∑k≥0​5−ksin(5kh). If 5m≤1/h<5m+1, the first m+1 terms have 0<5kh≤1 and contribute at least (m+1)hsin1, while the remaining tail has magnitude at most 5−m/4≤5h/4. This proves a lower modulus of continuity bound of order hlog(1/h) for small h. The inverse theorem for trigonometric approximation supplies the matching upper bound because the positive lacunary trigonometric series has En​(g)≍n−1.

Positive lacunary Chebyshev series (f=∑k≥0​ak​T3k​,En​(f)=∑3k>n​ak​)

Words: 76
Equioscillation theorem OurBigBook.com
For positive summable coefficients, the Weierstrass M-test gives a continuous uniform sum. The partial sum over 3k≤n is the unique best uniform approximation of degree at most n. If 3K is the first omitted frequency, every tail term equals (−1)j at xj​=cos(jπ/3K) because its frequency ratio is odd. The entire tail therefore attains alternating extrema equal in magnitude to its coefficient sum at more than n+1 points. The Chebyshev alternation theorem proves the assertion, including the empty partial sum at n=0.

Bernstein's lethargy theorem

Words: 100 Articles: 1
Uniform approximation OurBigBook.com
Bernstein's lethargy theorem says that best approximation errors in nested approximation spaces can tend to zero arbitrarily slowly. For algebraic polynomials on [−1,1], given any decreasing positive sequence δn​→0, there is a continuous function f whose best degree-n uniform-approximation error is at least δn​ for every n.

Let K be a compact Hausdorff space. A test subspace H⊂C(K,R) containing a strictly positive function is sufficient for uniform convergence of positive linear operators on continuous functions if, for each x∈K, the only positive linear functional agreeing with point evaluation on H is that evaluation itself. By the Riesz-Markov-Kakutani representation theorem, this is uniqueness of the positive measure with the prescribed moments. Boundedness from the positive test function and the Banach-Alaoglu theorem prove the assertion by compactness. The equality holds when an alternating unit-norm spline s∗​ has as many ordered extremal sites as the dimension, and those sites satisfy the Schoenberg–Whitney theorem. For every admissible set, sampling has operator norm at most one, giving κ(S)≤∥Ax−1​∥∞​. At the alternating sites the checkerboard inverse of a totally nonnegative matrix identifies each inverse absolute row sum with the magnitude of the corresponding coefficient of s∗​. The Chebyshev spline coefficient and dual norm equality therefore gives equality. This minimizes amplification into B-spline coefficients; it does not by itself prove optimality for the distinct Lebesgue constant of interpolation.

A finite collection of the standard partition-normalized B-splines is nonnegative and has sum at most one on the entire real line. Extend the knot sequence in both directions. The full order-one collection sums to one, and summing the Cox-de Boor recurrence preserves that sum because the two coefficients of each lower-order function add to one. The finite collection is a subset. On the basic knot interval the finite sum equals one, also following from Marsden's identity.
Simple-knot B-spline regularity (Ni,k​∈Ck−2,suppNi,k​=[ti​,ti+k​])

B-spline OurBigBook.com
For distinct increasing knots and k≥2, the explicit divided difference formula writes an order-k B-spline as a finite sum of truncated power functions of degree k−1. It is a piecewise polynomial function and is globally Ck−2. Below its first knot the order-k divided difference annihilates a degree-k−1 polynomial; above its last knot all values vanish. Nonzero first and last pieces give the exact closed support. Order one gives interval indicators instead of continuous splines.

An order-k B-spline is supported on [ti​,ti+k​]. Below this interval its truncated-power knot data agree with a degree-k−1 polynomial, annihilated by the order-k divided difference; above it all data vanish. Therefore its ordinary or mixed Gram matrix has entries zero when ∣i−j∣≥k. The half-bandwidth is k−1, and for strictly increasing knots this bound is sharp.

The projection maps continuous functions into the spline space, not onto all continuous functions.

Total nonnegativity of B-spline collocation matrices
Words: 106
B-spline collocation matrix OurBigBook.com
For increasing sites and an ordered nonnegative normalized B-spline basis, the matrix Aij​=Nj​(xi​) is a totally nonnegative matrix. One way to see the minors' signs is knot insertion. Each inserted knot changes coefficients by bj​=αj​aj​+(1−αj​)aj−1​ with 0≤αj​≤1, using the standard constant endpoint pieces. This is a nonnegative rectangular bidiagonal map, whose minors are nonnegative. Products preserve that property by the Cauchy–Binet formula. Insert each site to full knot multiplicity; a suitable refined coefficient is then the value s(xi​). Thus collocation is an ordered row submatrix of the refinement map, and has nonnegative minors. The strict support conditions ti​<xi​<ti+k​ give invertibility by the Schoenberg–Whitney theorem; its inverse has the checkerboard inverse of a totally nonnegative matrix sign pattern.

Schoenberg spline operator OurBigBook.com
For nonnegative partition-normalized order-k B-splines, let Vf(t)=∑i​f(τi​)Ni​(t) with each sample point inside [ti​,ti+k​]. If Ni​(t) is nonzero, both t and τi​ lie in an interval of length at most k∣Δ∣. Their function values differ by at most the modulus of continuity at that length. Summing with nonnegative weights of total one proves the displayed bound. With fixed order and vanishing maximum knot gap, uniform continuity gives uniform convergence. The same argument works for bounded piecewise-continuous outputs if full interior knot multiplicities are allowed; their individual continuity should not then be asserted.
